title: The calling sickness
summary: How spirits mark someone to become a shaman.

claims.text: Spirits that want a Sleeper to Awaken may send dream visits or reflections in mirrors, but most often they simply make the chosen person fall gravely ill.
The illness resists every cure, and it often lifts only once an older shaman notices it and takes the sufferer on as a student.

title: Sacred brews and visionary plants
summary: Plant medicines used to reach the Other Side.

claims.text: Shamans usually boil and steep visionary plants into a drink, and only the shaman prepares it, since many such plants are deadly when handled badly.
The recipes pass from teacher to student over generations; peyote and psilocybin mushrooms are the best known in North America, and peyote anchors a whole faith in the American southwest.
Laws against drug use have made these rites rarer, though attempts to stamp them out have mostly failed.

title: Shamans in the Umbra
summary: What changes when a shaman crosses into the spirit world.

claims.text: Once across the Gauntlet, a shaman's totem shows itself, familiars swell to at least double size unless their nature favors stealth, and spirits of the totem's Brood tend to show respect.
Long exposure brings bleedover, when spirit sights intrude on waking life; quiet meditation on the material side usually clears it.
A shaman who stays away from Earth for somewhere between four months and a year loses the body for good and becomes a spirit.

title: Bonds with a totem
summary: How shamans and totems choose each other.

claims.text: A totem embodies one drive or quality, and allying with one ties the shaman to that quality for life and sometimes after it.
The choice may come from a mentor, from the shaman, from the totem itself, or from the shaman's Avatar; most bonds form at the Awakening or during training.
A shaman never holds more than one totem, and a student's totem may differ entirely from the teacher's.
Some shamans treat the totem as an ideal to live up to, while others ally with it for help with one lifelong goal, such as freeing a conquered people.

title: Celestines and Incarna
summary: The great spirits above a shaman's reach.

claims.text: Celestines are pure archetypes of vast insight who grasp nothing outside their own nature, so any talk with one must be framed in its terms; ask a war god about pollution and it plans an attack.
Shamans therefore deal with Celestines only through distant worship or brief alliances, and look to the mightier but still understandable Incarna as patrons.

title: Jagglings and Gafflings
summary: The lesser ranks of the spirit world.

claims.text: Jagglings are the spirits who become shamans' familiars; curious ones wander into the material world and stir up trouble, sometimes with angry mages trailing behind.
Gafflings, the least spirits, have less free will, and shamans bind them into fetishes and talens.
Most fetish spirits chose that home: an object shields them from Umbral attack, lets them study the material world, and works much like a vow taken by a monk.
Fetishes speak to their owners, offering counsel or asking questions.
A fetish holds a spirit that powers it, such as a fire shirt that wards against burns or a snake staff that turns into a living serpent to guard the body while the spirit travels.
A talisman runs on Quintessence instead of a bound spirit; one well-known kind, a death mask, lets its wearer see wraiths and enter the Shadowlands through deep water or below ground.

title: Mages taught by spirits
summary: Shamans Awakened with no human teacher.

claims.text: A few mages are Awakened and trained by a spirit rather than a person, and they tend to be cut off from other mages and to hold odd ideas about them.
Dreamspeakers hold that spirits Awaken such mages as tools for some purpose, and a patron with a hidden aim may feed its student falsehoods.
